Sunlight is made up of all colors, but it travels through the atmosphere as a mix of wavelengths. Air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths—like blue and violet—much more strongly than longer ones, a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering. This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all directions, so the sky looks blue during the day.
